purpose: Pin what `$ErrorActionPreference` changes, so the frontend's decision to skip it is checked against a measurement rather than against a reading of the documentation.
note: The frontend lowers external command invocations, assignments of literal text, and `&&` chains. `$ErrorActionPreference` reaches none of them: a failing external command does not stop the script under either setting. It reaches a cmdlet, and there it decides whether the script stops. So skipping the statement is sound exactly while every cmdlet is refused, which `a_powershell_cmdlet_is_still_refused` is what holds. A case marked `differs` is one where the setting changes the program.
